classification.difficultyReason: Calculate progressive tax, express it as a percentage of income and reverse the bracket calculations.

inlines.text: This question uses the income tax rates in the nation of Immutatia, which are as follows.
There is no tax on the first $12 000 that a person earns in any one year.
From $12 001 to $30 000, the tax rate is 15c for each dollar over $12 000.
From $30 001 to $75 000, the tax rate is 25c for each dollar over $30 000.
Over $75 000, the tax rate is 35c for each dollar over $75 000.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the income tax payable on:

answer.worked: The income is below the tax-free threshold of $\$12\,000$, so no income tax is payable.

The first $\$12\,000$ is tax-free.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Tax on next }\$18\,000&=18\,000\times0.15\\\text{Tax on next }\$18\,000&=\$2700\\\text{Tax on remaining }\$6000&=6000\times0.25\\\text{Tax on remaining }\$6000&=\$1500\\\text{Total tax}&=2700+1500\\\text{Total tax}&=\$4200\end{align*}$$

The first $\$12\,000$ is tax-free.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Tax on next }\$18\,000&=18\,000\times0.15\\\text{Tax on next }\$18\,000&=\$2700\\\text{Tax on next }\$45\,000&=45\,000\times0.25\\\text{Tax on next }\$45\,000&=\$11\,250\\\text{Tax on remaining }\$125\,000&=125\,000\times0.35\\\text{Tax on remaining }\$125\,000&=\$43\,750\\\text{Total tax}&=2700+11\,250+43\,750\\\text{Total tax}&=\$57\,700\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: What percentage, to 2 decimal places, of each person’s income was paid in income tax in parts i–iv of part a?

answer.worked:
For each person, divide the tax by the income and multiply by $100\%$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{i: percentage}&=\frac{0}{8000}\times100\%=0.00\%\\\text{ii: percentage}&=\frac{300}{14\,000}\times100\%\approx2.14\%\\\text{iii: percentage}&=\frac{4200}{36\,000}\times100\%\approx11.67\%\\\text{iv: percentage}&=\frac{57\,700}{200\,000}\times100\%=28.85\%\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the income if the income tax on it was:

answer.worked:
Tax up to $\$30\,000$ is $18\,000\times0.15=\$2700$, so this income is in the 15% bracket.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Income above }\$12\,000&=1260\div0.15\\\text{Income above }\$12\,000&=\$8400\\\text{Income}&=12\,000+8400\\\text{Income}&=\$20\,400\end{align*}$$

Tax on the first $\$30\,000$ is $\$2700$; tax on the first $\$75\,000$ is $\$13\,950$. This income is in the 25% bracket.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Tax above }\$30\,000&=3420-2700\\\text{Tax above }\$30\,000&=\$720\\\text{Income above }\$30\,000&=720\div0.25\\\text{Income above }\$30\,000&=\$2880\\\text{Income}&=30\,000+2880\\\text{Income}&=\$32\,880\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\text{Tax through }\$30\,000&=18\,000\times0.15\\\text{Tax through }\$30\,000&=\$2700\\\text{Tax through }\$75\,000&=2700+45\,000\times0.25\\\text{Tax through }\$75\,000&=\$13\,950\end{align*}$$
Therefore the income is $\$75\,000$.

Tax on the first $\$75\,000$ is $2700+11\,250=\$13\,950$. The remaining tax is charged at 35%.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Tax above }\$75\,000&=14\,650-13\,950\\\text{Tax above }\$75\,000&=\$700\\\text{Income above }\$75\,000&=700\div0.35\\\text{Income above }\$75\,000&=\$2000\\\text{Income}&=75\,000+2000\\\text{Income}&=\$77\,000\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: One six-year loan attracts compound interest calculated at $2\%$, $4\%$, $6\%$, $8\%$, $10\%$ and $12\%$ in successive years. Another six-year loan attracts compound interest calculated at $12\%$, $10\%$, $8\%$, $6\%$, $4\%$ and $2\%$ in successive years. Find the total percentage increase in money owing in both cases, correct to 2 decimal places, compare the two results, and explain what has happened.

answer.short:
$49.61\%$ for both loans.

Reversing the order of the annual multipliers does not change their product.
answer.worked:
For the first loan:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Final amount}&=\text{original amount}\times1.02\times1.04\times1.06\times1.08\times1.10\times1.12\\\text{Final amount}&=\text{original amount}\times1.49614553088\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Final amount}&=\text{original amount}\times1.12\times1.10\times1.08\times1.06\times1.04\times1.02\\\text{Final amount}&=\text{original amount}\times1.49614553088\end{aligned}$$
Thus, for each loan:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Percentage increase}&=(1.49614553088-1)\times100\%\\\text{Percentage increase}&\approx49.61\%\end{aligned}$$
Both loans have the same percentage increase because multiplication is commutative: changing the order of the annual multipliers does not change their product.

Everything in this chapter involves calculations with percentages. We are now assuming that you are using a calculator, so we have made little attempt to set questions where the numbers work out nicely. However, some of the problems can be done mentally. entries.description:
When money is lent by a bank, whoever borrows the money normally makes a payment, called interest, for the use of the money.
The amount of interest paid depends on:
• the principal, which is the amount of money borrowed
• the rate at which interest is charged
• the time for which the money is borrowed.
Conversely, if a person invests money in a bank or elsewhere, the bank pays the person interest because the bank uses the money to finance its own investments.
This section will deal only with simple interest. In simple interest transactions, interest is paid on the original amount borrowed.

entries.description:
How much simple interest will I pay altogether if I borrow $4000 for 10 years at an interest rate of 7% per annum? (The phrase per annum is Latin for ‘for each year’; it is often abbreviated to p.a.)
Last year you probably learned to set out the working for simple interest in two successive steps, something like this:

Interest paid at the end of each year = 4000 × 7%
= 4000 × 0.07
= $280

= $2800

entries.description:
This working can all be done in one step if we can develop a suitable formula.
Suppose I borrow $P for T years at an interest rate R. Using the same two-step approach as before:

Interest paid at the end of each year = P × R

Total interest paid over T years = P × R × T
= PRT

entries.description:

I = PRT    (Interest = principal × rate × time)

Calculations involving brackets can be tricky to handle when using the calculator.
For example, working with the figures in the summary box above, suppose that a population has increased by 15%, 24% and 38% in three successive years and is now 50 000. Then:
original population = 50 000 ÷ (1.15 × 1.24 × 1.38)

original population = 50 000 ÷ (1.15 × 1.24 × 1.38)
